why: Anyone who wants to try the project should be able to copy and run the commands in order. Miss one step and they get stuck and move on.
question: How do I run this on my computer?
who: Required for all four project types

parts.heading: ### Requirements
parts.text: Start with what must be installed and which version. Give a number like "Node.js 22", not "latest version".
parts.emphasis: Versions must match the project configuration files.

parts.heading: ### Installation
parts.text: Start from cloning the repository, one command per line, so pasting them in order gets the project running.
parts.emphasis: End with the local URL to open and what the reader should see when it works.

parts.heading: ### Running Tests
parts.text: Only needed if the project has tests; just show the command to run them.

lines.text: Please install the [[latest version]] of Node.js.
Then [[open your browser]] to see the page.

notes.title: Says "latest version"
notes.text: That changes in six months; write a specific number.

notes.title: Commands start with $
notes.text: Copying includes the $ prompt and the command fails.

notes.title: Commands mismatch the project
notes.text: The project uses pnpm and has no serve script.

notes.title: No URL or expected result
notes.text: Give the local URL and what shows it worked.

lines: Open http://localhost:5173. You should see the menu.

tip.title: Paste and run your own steps once
paragraphs: Open a fresh folder and paste every line from top to bottom. Wherever it fails is where a step is missing.
If AI writes the README for you, it runs the checker afterwards and fixes commands that do not match the project.

types.web-app: Include the local URL to open once the dev server starts.
types.course-example: Say which branch to start on and where the finished version lives. Write the steps in the exact order students follow.
types.portfolio: Keep the steps short, but make sure they actually work—interviewers sometimes run them.
types.backend-api: Add a Database Setup section and keep the start command for Usage: install, set up the database, then start, so pasting top to bottom works.
